nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, or small indel variants in PCNT (21q22.3) abolish production of functional pericentrin, an unusually large coiled-coil scaffold protein of the pericentriolar material. Sequence analysis detects the great majority of pathogenic alleles; missense variants are a minor contributor. Some individuals originally reported as having Seckel syndrome carry PCNT loss-of-function variants and are, on review, clinically compatible with MOPD II.

nodes.description: Pericentrin anchors both structural and regulatory proteins at the centrosome, including gamma-tubulin ring complexes that nucleate spindle microtubules. Its absence disorganizes the mitotic spindle and causes chromosome missegregation in dividing cells. This node substitutes PCNT for the generic centrosome/spindle lesion of the neural progenitor centrosome-spindle module.

nodes.description: Beyond the growth deficit, MOPD II carries a distinctive systemic vasculopathy affecting the intracranial, coronary, renal, and external carotid circulations. Neurovascular disease (moyamoya vasculopathy and intracranial aneurysms) is the leading cause of premature death; moyamoya tends to present earlier than aneurysms, and aneurysm risk persists across the shortened lifespan. Hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and premature coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction in young adults complete the picture. This is a parallel arm that is not fully explained by the proliferation deficit alone; the intervening cell biology is curated as an explicit knowledge gap rather than asserted.

nodes.description: Impaired mitotic fidelity and checkpoint signaling reduce the proliferative output of rapidly dividing progenitor pools during embryonic and fetal development — neural progenitors in the cortical germinal zones, and growth plate chondrocytes and osteoblasts in the skeleton. Because the lesion is in a ubiquitously required mitotic apparatus rather than a tissue-restricted program, the deficit is global rather than organ-selective, which is what makes the resulting growth failure "primordial" (prenatal in onset and never caught up).
